evidence.title: External trigeminal nerve stimulation in youth with ADHD: a randomized, sham-controlled, phase 2b trial (PMID 41545587; Nat Med 2026 Feb;32(2):582-590; Epub 2026 Jan 16)
External trigeminal nerve stimulation in youth with ADHD: a randomized, sham-controlled, phase 2b trial
External trigeminal nerve stimulation in youth with ADHD: a randomized, sham-controlled, phase 2b trial (full text, PMC12920111)
Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation for ADHD (NCT02155608): pivotal double-blind sham-controlled trial, 62 randomized, results posted 2019-04-12
Efficacy of Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation for ADHD (NCT05374187): randomized, 218 enrolled, completed, no results posted

outcomes.note: Criterion: first PubMed-indexed publication or ClinicalTrials.gov posting dated after 2026-01-15 reporting primary results of an RCT of the Monarch eTNS in youth ADHD (or refractory seizures), designed to test the efficacy finding behind the FDA clearance and randomizing more participants than the pivotal trial (McGough 2019, NCT02155608, 62 randomized). Conti et al., Nature Medicine 32(2):582-590, published online 2026-01-16 (PubMed Epub 2026 Jan 16, PMID 41545587): multicentre double-blind sham-controlled phase 2b ATTENS trial (ISRCTN82129325) of the Monarch TNS System (NeuroSigma), 150 randomized (75/75), explicitly a confirmatory test of the pilot; primary outcome (parent ADHD-RS at 4 weeks) showed no differential effect (adjusted mean difference 0.83, P=0.622). Direction is irrelevant. No earlier registry results posting exists (UCLA NCT05374187, n=218, has none). Date = 2026-01-16.

outcomes.note: The trial is identified as COMBAT-SI (NCT05377177, UC San Diego, PI Cory Weissman): the only registered randomized comparison of bilateral versus unilateral (accelerated theta burst) stimulation for suicidal ideation, funded by NIMH career-development award K23MH138746, a 'K award', which matches the forecaster's 'Kale Award'. As of 2026-09-13 the registry shows status Recruiting, no results posted, estimated primary completion 2029-08-01; PubMed has no publication of its primary outcome, and no other bilateral-vs-unilateral suicidal-ideation RCT has reported. Not occurred as of the check date. The link to Paul Fitzgerald's Brain Stimulation 2025 session could not be verified; if the forecaster meant another trial, the identification can be challenged.

evidence.title: BrainsWay Announces First Coverage Policy for Accelerated Deep TMS (Premera policy covering the SWIFT protocol)

outcomes.note: Premera Blue Cross policy 2.01.526 lists 'Accelerated intensive TMS' (more than one treatment daily) as medically necessary for a full intensive course of standard or deep TMS when criteria for that TMS type are met; its medically necessary indications include bipolar depression and OCD (deep and standard TMS). The current version (effective 2026-08-01) allows up to 5 treatments/day and names the deep TMS SWIFT protocol medically necessary when deep TMS criteria are met. The archived version effective 2024-04-04 already made 2 treatments daily medically necessary under hardship conditions for all covered indications. The policy history dates the accelerated intensive TMS criteria and OCD coverage to 2023-02-03; that version's text was not retrievable, so the date rests on the history plus the unchanged 2024 text. No policy found for PTSD or ADHD. This predates the forecaster's statement.

outcomes.note: No 510(k) clearance, De Novo grant or PMA approval of a transcranial magnetic stimulation device with ADHD in its indications for use is dated by 2026-09-13. FDA product-code classifications for ADHD devices are limited to QGL (transcutaneous trigeminal nerve stimulator, the Monarch eTNS, De Novo 2019) and QFT (digital therapeutic software); the seven TMS product codes (OBP, SIG, QFF, SGE, QCI, OKP, QMD) cover MDD, PTSD, OCD, migraine and smoking cessation, not ADHD. None of the 89 TMS 510(k) records (latest K260691, decided 2026-08-23) or the three TMS-related De Novo grants names ADHD, and openFDA lists no TMS PMA. Trials, publications and off-label use do not count.
